                   ; COMP80 CALC                   ;                   ; A spreadsheet for the PSI COMP80, after VisiCalc (1979), in the 2 KB of                   ; ROM (0400h-0BFFh) that held BURP.  The monitor (0000h-03FFh) is                   ; unchanged.  As with BURP, the RS key enters it: the monitor's NMI handler                   ; jumps to 0800h.                   ;                   ; The sheet is 6 columns, A-F, of 10 characters and 24 rows.  Each line                   ; typed goes into the cell marked >, which then moves down (or right, after                   ; /R):                   ;   123.45  -6  +A1*B2  (A1+A2)/2  @SUM(A1...A5)   a value: a formula                   ;   RENT  "123                                     a label (a letter or ")                   ;   >B3                                            go to B3                   ;   /B blank  /C clear all  /D /R move down or right  /F0-2 decimals                   ;   /U copy the cell above, /L the cell on the left, moving its references                   ;   down or right (a column or row with $ in front stays as it is: $A1 B$2)                   ; An empty line just moves on.                   ;                   ; Numbers are 32-bit fixed point in hundredths: -21474836.48 to 21474836.47,                   ; with two decimals.  * and / work through a 64-bit product, rounded.                   ; Formulas have the usual precedence, brackets, cell references A1-F24 and                   ; @SUM of a range (the @ is optional).  Labels and empty cells count as 0.  After every                   ; change all the formulas are worked out again, row by row, until nothing                   ; changes (8 times at most, for references to cells further on).  A formula                   ; that can't be worked out shows ERROR, and so does any that uses it.                   ;                   ; Each cell is 32 bytes: its kind (0 empty, 1 label, 2 value, 3 error), its                   ; value (4 bytes, low first) and its text (27 bytes with the 0).                   ;                   ; Keys are handled as in COMP80 FORTH: the monitor's NMI handler echoes each                   ; key and wakes the HALT in RAWKEY; RS while waiting is a rubout and RS at                   ; any other time (re)starts CALC, keeping the sheet.  Any key while it is                   ; working resets to the monitor; RS comes back with the sheet kept.                    VRAM:   equ 8000h                   MAGIC:  equ 0C00h           ; MAGICV when the sheet below is valid                   CURS:   equ 0C02h           ; output position in screen memory                   ROW:    equ 0C04h           ; the cell marked: row 0-23,                   COL:    equ 0C05h           ; column 0-5                   DIRN:   equ 0C06h           ; 0 move down, 1 move right                   DEC:    equ 0C07h           ; decimals shown, 0-2                   ERRSP:  equ 0C08h           ; stack to go back to on an error                   CHG:    equ 0C0Ah           ; something changed in this pass                   TYPN:   equ 0C0Bh           ; a cell's new kind,                   OPB:    equ 0C0Ch           ; and value; the right operand                   XV:     equ 0C10h           ; |left|                   YV:     equ 0C14h           ; the multiplier                   ZV:     equ 0C18h           ; the divisor                   PV:     equ 0C1Ch           ; the 64-bit product; quotient and remainder                   RLO:    equ 0C26h           ; range: first row, first column                   RHI:    equ 0C28h           ;        last row, last column                   CR:     equ 0C2Ah           ; the cell being added in                   CC:     equ 0C2Bh                   SGN:    equ 0C2Ch           ; (in * and /) the sign of the answer                   TIB:    equ 0C40h           ; the line typed (26 characters and a 0)                   NEND:   equ 0C70h           ; numbers are formatted backwards from here                   CELLS:  equ 0C80h           ; 144 cells of 32 bytes, to 1E80h                   S0:     equ 1F00h           ; stack (the monitor uses 1Fxx)                   MAGICV: equ 0CA1Ch                            org 0400h                    ; ---------------------------------------------------------------- arithmetic                   ;                    ; COMP80 TRAC                   ;                   ; TRAC, Calvin Mooers' Text Reckoning And Compiling language of 1964, in the                   ; style of TRAC T-64, for the PSI COMP80, in the 2 KB of ROM (0400h-0BFFh)                   ; that held BURP.  The monitor (0000h-03FFh) is unchanged.  As with BURP, the                   ; RS key enters it: the monitor's NMI handler jumps to 0800h.                   ;                   ; Everything is a string.  The processor scans the active string a character                   ; at a time and builds the neutral string:                   ;   (    protects: everything up to the matching ) goes to the neutral string                   ;        unscanned, without the outer parentheses                   ;   CR   is deleted                   ;   ,    ends an argument                   ;   #(   starts an active function: its value goes back into the active                   ;        string to be scanned again                   ;   ##(  starts a neutral function: its value goes into the neutral string                   ;   )    ends a function, which is then evaluated                   ; When the active string is empty the idling procedure #(PS,#(RS)) is                   ; loaded again: RS reads what is typed, up to the meta character (' to begin                   ; with), and the result of scanning it is printed.                   ;                   ; Primitives (names in capitals; a missing argument is the null string):                   ;   PS,X         print X                     RS       read up to the meta char                   ;   RC           read one character          CM,X     meta character = X                   ;   DS,N,X       define form N as X          SS,N,X1,X2...  mark X1, X2... in                   ;   CL,N,A1,A2.. N with its segment gaps          N as segment gaps 1, 2...                   ;                filled by A1, A2...                   ;   CS,N,Z       the next segment of N, or Z at its end                   ;   CC,N,Z       the next character of N, or Z at its end                   ;   IN,N,X,Z     N from its form pointer up to X (the pointer moves past X),                   ;                or Z if X isn't there                   ;   CR,N         form pointer back to the start                   ;   DD,N1,N2...  delete forms              DA       delete all forms                   ;   AD SU ML DV,A,B,Z  A+B, A-B, A*B, A/B: the numbers at the ends of A and                   ;                B, with A's prefix in front; DV by 0 gives Z                   ;   EQ,A,B,T,F   T if A and B are the same, otherwise F                   ;   GR,A,B,T,F   T if the number in A is greater than the one in B, else F                   ;   LN,S         the names of the forms, each after S                   ;   PF,N         print form N, its gaps shown as <1>, <2>...                   ; Numbers are 16-bit integers.  An unknown function has the null value.                   ;                   ; A form is kept from FORMS as: length of the record (2), form pointer (2),                   ; name, 0, body, 0.  In the body a byte 80h+i is segment gap i.                   ;                   ; Keys and screen are as in FORTH: the monitor's NMI handler echoes each key                   ; at (DE); RS while waiting for a key is rubout; any key while TRAC is busy                   ; resets to the monitor and RS comes back with the forms kept.  Line 0 shows                   ; TRAC, lines 1-31 scroll.                    MAGIC:  equ 0C00h           ; MAGICV when the forms below are valid                   FEND:   equ 0C02h           ; end of the forms                   META:   equ 0C04h           ; the meta character                   CURS:   equ 0C06h           ; output position in screen memory                   NP:     equ 0C08h           ; end of the neutral string                   AP:     equ 0C0Ah           ; scan point in the active string                   VB:     equ 0C0Ch           ; where a function builds its value                   FMARK:  equ 0C0Eh           ; the function's marker in the neutral string                   FREC:   equ 0C10h           ; form being worked on                   PFXE:   equ 0C12h           ; end of the first argument's prefix                   SSI:    equ 0C14h           ; SS: argument number                   SSP:    equ 0C16h           ; SS: the string to mark                   INS:    equ 0C18h           ; IN: where the value starts                   MODE:   equ 0C1Ah           ; F1h active function, F2h neutral                   ARGC:   equ 0C1Bh                   ARGV:   equ 0C1Ch           ; 16 argument pointers                   FORMS:  equ 0C40h                   FTOP:   equ 1400h           ; the forms must end below here                   NBASE:  equ 1400h           ; the neutral string grows up from here,                   AEND:   equ 1C00h           ; the active string down from here                   RSBUF:  equ 1C00h           ; what RS reads                   RSEND:  equ 1DF0h                   S0:     equ 1F00h           ; machine stack (the monitor uses 1Fxx)                   MAGICV: equ 07A3Ch                   MAXARG: equ 16                    ACTF:   equ 0F1h            ; marks in the neutral string                   NEUF:   equ 0F2h                   ARGSEP: equ 0F3h                    VRAM:   equ 8000h                   CLS64:  equ 0393h           ; monitor: spaces from 8040h to the end of the screen                   PAD64:  equ 03C4h           ;                    ; COMP80 PL/0                   ;                   ; A compiler for PL/0, Niklaus Wirth's teaching language, in the 2 KB of ROM                   ; (0400h-0BFFh) that held BURP.  The monitor (0000h-03FFh) is unchanged.  As                   ; with BURP, the RS key enters it: the monitor's NMI handler jumps to 0800h.                   ;                   ; The program is typed in numbered lines and kept as typed, as in COMP80                   ; BASIC: each line its number (2 bytes, low first), its text and 0Dh, from                   ; 0C04h up to TXTEND.  RUN compiles the whole program in one pass, by                   ; recursive descent, straight into Z80 machine code after the text, and                   ; calls it.  CODE compiles it and says how long the code is.                   ;                   ;   program   = block "." .                   ;   block     = [CONST name = number {, name = number} ;]                   ;               [VAR name {, name} ;]                   ;               {PROCEDURE name ; block ;} statement .                   ;   statement = [name := expression | CALL name | ? name | ! expression                   ;               | BEGIN statement {; statement} END | IF condition THEN                   ;               statement | WHILE condition DO statement                   ;               | PLOT expression , expression | CLS] .                   ;   condition = ODD expression | expression (= # < <= > >=) expression .                   ;   expression = [-] term {(+|-) term} .                   ;   term      = factor {(*|/) factor} .                   ;   factor    = name | number | ( expression ) .                   ;                   ; Names follow the blocks they are declared in, but every variable has one                   ; place in memory (1C00h up), so a procedure that calls itself shares its                   ; variables with itself, as in FORTRAN.                   ;                   ; Code: an expression leaves its value in HL.  A number is LD HL,n and a                   ; variable LD HL,(v); an operator is PUSH HL, the right operand, POP DE and                   ; the operation on DE and HL (ADD HL,DE, or a call for * / and the                   ; comparisons).  When the right operand is a single load, the PUSH becomes                   ; EX DE,HL and there is no POP.  Assignment is LD (v),HL; IF and WHILE test                   ; with LD A,H / OR L / JP Z; CALL is CALL; a procedure ends with RET.  A block                   ; jumps over its procedures to its statement.                   ;                   ; Keys and screen are handled as in COMP80 BASIC and FORTH: the monitor's                   ; NMI handler echoes each key and wakes the HALT in RAWKEY; RS while waiting                   ; is a rubout and RS at any other time (re)starts PL/0, keeping the program.                   ; Any key while a program runs resets to the monitor; RS comes back with the                   ; program kept.  Line 0 shows PL/0; lines 1-31 scroll.                    VRAM:   equ 8000h                   CLS64:  equ 0393h           ; monitor: spaces from 8040h to the end of the screen                   PAD64:  equ 03C4h           ; monitor: spaces at (DE) up to the next line                    MAGIC:  equ 0C00h           ; MAGICV when the program below is valid                   TXTEND: equ 0C02h           ; end of the program text; the code follows it                   PROG:   equ 0C04h           ; first line                   MAGICV: equ 0A0F0h                   TOPH:   equ 18h             ; the text ends below 1800h                   CODEH:  equ 1Ah             ; the code ends below 1A00h                   SYMS:   equ 1A00h           ; names: the name (80h on its last letter),                   SYMH:   equ 1Ch             ;   its kind (0 CONST, 1 VAR, 2 PROCEDURE)                   VARS:   equ 1C00h           ;   and its value; then the variables                   TIB:    equ 1D00h           ; input line (80 bytes; page aligned)                   IDBUF:  equ 1D50h           ; the last name read (80 bytes)                   CURS:   equ 1DA0h           ; output position in screen memory                   LINEP:  equ 1DA2h           ; the line being compiled, 0 if none                   SRCP:   equ 1DA4h           ; where the compiler is reading                   TOK:    equ 1DA6h           ; the token just read                   TOKV:   equ 1DA7h           ; its value, for a number                   CODEP:  equ 1DA9h           ; where the next byte of code goes                   SYMEND: equ 1DABh           ; end of the names                   VARP:   equ 1DADh           ; the next free variable                   KEYBUF: equ 1DC0h           ; digits and keys while KEY waits                   S0:     equ 1F00h           ; stack (monitor uses 1Fxx)                    ; Tokens: 0 end of the text, 1 a name, 2 a number, 3 :=, 4 <=, 5 >=, the                   ; As with BURP, the RS key                   ; enters it: the monitor's NMI handler jumps to 0800h.                   ;                   ; The language has eight commands; every other character is a comment.                   ;                   ;   >  move the data pointer one cell right     <  one cell left                   ;   +  add 1 to the cell                        -  take 1 from it                   ;   .  print the cell as a character            ,  read a key into it                   ;   [  if the cell is 0, jump past the matching ]                   ;   ]  if the cell is not 0, jump back to the command after the matching [                   ;                   ; Cells are bytes and wrap round (255 + 1 is 0); so does the tape at its                   ; ends.  The tape is 768 cells at 1A00h, or 30000 at 8800h with the 32 KB                   ; expansion.  All eight characters can be typed on the COMP80 keyboard.                   ;                   ; Programs are typed as numbered lines, as in BASIC: a number on its own                   ; deletes that line.  LIST, NEW, RUN (flat out), SHOW (the program, the tape                   ; and the output on the screen as it runs, SPEED n setting the pause between                   ; commands) and STEP (the same, one command a key: Q stops, R runs on at                   ; SPEED).  A line typed without a number runs at once, flat out.                   ;                   ; RUN first copies the commands out of the program into CODE, one byte                   ; each, and finds the matching brackets: MATCH holds, for each [ and ], the                   ; address of its partner in CODE.                   ;                   ; Output: 10 is a new line, 32-95 print as themselves, 96-127 as capitals,                   ; and 128 + n prints graphics character n (143 is a solid block).  A key                   ; read by , is shown, and Return gives 10.                   ;                   ; Keys and screen are as in FORTH: the monitor's NMI handler echoes each key                   ; at (DE); RS while waiting for a key is rubout; any key while a program runs                   ; resets to the monitor and RS comes back with the program kept.  Line 0                   ; shows BF, lines 1-31 scroll.                    MAGIC:  equ 0C00h           ; MAGICV when the program below is valid                   PEND:   equ 0C02h           ; end of the program                   SPEED:  equ 0C04h           ; SHOW's pause, about 0.8 ms a unit (20 at first)                   PROG:   equ 0C06h           ; first program line                   PTOP:   equ 1400h           ; the program must end below here                   MAGICV: equ 0BF0Fh                    CODE:   equ 1400h           ; the commands, one byte each, then 0                   CODEND: equ 1600h           ; so at most 511 of them                   MATCH:  equ 1600h           ; for each command, its partner if a bracket                   TAPES:  equ 1A00h           ; the tape without the expansion: 768 cells                   TAPESE: equ 1D00h                   TAPEX:  equ 8800h           ; with it: 30000 cells                   TAPEXE: equ 8800h+30000                    TIB:    equ 1D00h           ; input line (80 bytes)                   TAPE0:  equ 1D50h           ; first cell                   TEND:   equ 1D52h           ; past the last cell                   CP:     equ 1D54h           ; end of CODE while copying                   MODE:   equ 1D56h           ; 0 RUN, 1 SHOW, 2 STEP                   STEPS:  equ 1D58h           ; commands run                   PAGE:   equ 1D5Ah           ; which 256 commands are on the screen                   OMARK:  equ 1D5Ch           ; where the command marker is                   TOP:    equ 1D5Eh           ; first line that scrolls                   IPV:    equ 1D60h           ; IP and DP, kept for the display                   DPV:    equ 1D62h                   CURS:   equ 1DA0h           ; output position in screen memory                   S0:     equ 1F00h           ; machine stack (the monitor uses 1Fxx)                    VRAM:   equ 8000h                   CLS64:  equ 0393h           ; monitor: spaces from 8040h to the end of the screen                   PAD64:  equ 03C4h           ; monitor: spaces at (DE) up to the next line                   MARK:   equ 43h             ; upper half block: the markers                    ROWST:  equ VRAM+1*64       ; status line                   ROWCD:  equ VRAM+2*64       ; code on lines 2, 4, 6, 8; markers below each                   ROWTL:  equ VRAM+11*64      ; tape label                   ROWTP:  equ VRAM+12*64      ; 16 cells, marker on the line below                   ROWOL:  equ VRAM+14*64      ; output label                   ROWOUT: equ VRAM+15*64      ; output, scrolling, to the bottom                            org 0400h                    ; ---------------------------------------------------------------- terminal                    ;                    ; COMP80 ED                   ;                   ; A line editor in the style of the Unix ed and the editors of its time,                   ; written for the PSI COMP80 in the 2 KB of ROM (0400h-0BFFh) that held                   ; BURP.  The monitor (0000h-03FFh) is unchanged.  As with BURP, the RS key                   ; enters it: the monitor's NMI handler jumps to 0800h.                   ;                   ; The text is a list of lines, each ending in 0Dh, with a 0 after the last.                   ; There is a current line, dot.  A command is an optional address or range                   ; and a letter:                   ;   addresses  n  .  $  /PATTERN/ (the next line containing it, wrapping)                   ;              +n and -n after any of them, or alone (from dot);                   ;              a,b is a range; , or % alone is 1,$                   ;   A  I  C    append after, insert before, change: lines typed in until                   ;              one that is just a full stop                   ;   D P N      delete, print, print with numbers                   ;   V          view the 30 lines round dot (or the address), > at it                   ;   M d  T d   move or copy the range to after line d                   ;   J          join (default . and the next)                   ;   S/OLD/NEW/ change the first OLD in each line; G after it, every one                   ;   G/PAT/cmd  run cmd on each line containing PAT (P if there is none)                   ;   =          the line number ($ unless an address is given)                   ;   E          empty the buffer;  W  how to save it on tape;  R  take in a                   ;              buffer read from tape;  Q  the monitor                   ;   an address alone prints that line; Return alone, the next one.                   ; Mistakes print ? and what was wrong.  A key while ED is busy resets to the                   ; monitor; RS comes back with the text kept.                   ;                   ; The text is kept from BEG to the 0 at ENDP, and must end below TOP: from                   ; 0C10h to 1BFFh, or 8800h-FFEFh with the 32 KB expansion.  The header at                   ; 0C00h keeps it over a reset.  Keys and screen are handled as in COMP80                   ; FORTH and VTL-2: line 0 shows ED; lines 1-31 scroll.                    VRAM:   equ 8000h                   CLS64:  equ 0393h           ; monitor: spaces from 8040h to the end of the screen                   PAD64:  equ 03C4h           ; monitor: spaces at (DE) up to the next line                    MAGIC:  equ 0C00h           ; MAGICV when the buffer below is valid                   ENDP:   equ 0C02h           ; the 0 after the last line                   BEG:    equ 0C04h           ; first line                   TOP:    equ 0C06h           ; the text must end below here                   DOT:    equ 0C08h           ; the current line                   MAGICV: equ 0EDEDh                   SMALL:  equ 0C10h                    TIB2:   equ 1C00h           ; a line being built by S (128 bytes)                   TIB:    equ 1D00h           ; input line (80 bytes; page aligned)                   PAT:    equ 1D50h           ; S's pattern, ended by 0Dh                   CURS:   equ 1DA0h           ; output position in screen memory                   L1:     equ 1DA2h           ; the range                   L2:     equ 1DA4h                   NADR:   equ 1DA6h           ; how many addresses were given (byte)                   TMPA:   equ 1DAAh                   TMPS:   equ 1DACh                   GN:     equ 1DAEh           ; G: the line it is at                   GOLD:   equ 1DB0h           ; G: the lines before the command                   NUMF:   equ 1DB2h           ; print with numbers (byte)                   SFLAG:  equ 1DB3h           ; S: something changed (byte), and G (bit 1)                   DEST:   equ 1DB4h                   REP:    equ 1C80h           ; S's replacement (80 bytes)                   GCMD:   equ 1E00h           ; G's command (80 bytes)                   GPAT:   equ 1E50h           ; G's pattern (48 bytes)                   S0:     equ 1F00h           ; stack (monitor uses 1Fxx)                            org 0400h                    ;                    ; COMP80 FILE                   ;                   ; A little card-file database for the PSI COMP80, in the 2 KB of ROM                   ; (0400h-0BFFh) that held BURP.  The monitor (0000h-03FFh) is unchanged.  As                   ; with BURP, the RS key enters it: the monitor's NMI handler jumps to 0800h.                   ;                   ;   FIELDS NAME,TOWN,AGE      names the fields (up to 8)                   ;   ADD SMITH,LEEDS,42        adds a card                   ;   LIST [WHERE ...]          the cards as a table, numbered                   ;   FIND TEXT                 the cards with TEXT anywhere in them                   ;   SHOW n                    card n in full                   ;   SORT BY FIELD [DESC]      sorts the cards                   ;   COUNT [WHERE ...]         how many cards                   ;   SUM FIELD [WHERE ...]     adds up a field;  AVG FIELD [WHERE ...]                   ;   DELETE n, DELETE WHERE ...                   ;   NEW                       clears everything                   ; WHERE takes up to four conditions FIELD op VALUE joined by AND or OR,                   ; worked out from left to right; op is = < > <> <= >=, and a * at the end                   ; of VALUE matches any ending.  Fields that are both numbers compare as                   ; numbers, others as text.  Numbers may have two decimals: they are kept                   ; as 32-bit hundredths.                   ;                   ; The cards are kept as typed, one line each: the fields with commas                   ; between them and 0Dh at the end, from RECS up to RECEND.  The field                   ; names are a line of the same kind at FLDS.  So TAPE 0C00 <RECEND> saves                   ; the whole file.                   ;                   ; Keys and screen are handled as in COMP80 FORTH: the monitor's NMI handler                   ; echoes each key and wakes the HALT in RAWKEY; RS while waiting is a                   ; rubout, and RS at any other time (re)starts FILE with the cards kept.                   ; Line 0 shows COMP80 FILE; lines 1-31 scroll.                    VRAM:   equ 8000h                   CLS64:  equ 0393h           ; monitor: spaces from 8040h to the end of the screen                   PAD64:  equ 03C4h           ; monitor: spaces at (DE) up to the next line                    MAGIC:  equ 0C00h           ; MAGICV when the file below is valid                   RECEND: equ 0C02h           ; end of the cards                   NF:     equ 0C04h           ; number of fields                   FLDS:   equ 0C05h           ; field names, NAME,TOWN,...0Dh (to 0C3Fh)                   RECS:   equ 0C40h           ; first card                   MAGICV: equ 0F11Eh                   TOP:    equ 1C00h           ; the cards end below here                   MAXF:   equ 8                    TIB:    equ 1D00h           ; input line (80 bytes; page aligned)                   CURS:   equ 1DA0h           ; output position in screen memory                   RECNO:  equ 1DA2h           ; number of the card being looked at                   NCOND:  equ 1DA4h           ; conditions in CONDS                   MODE:   equ 1DA5h           ; 0: match by CONDS; 1: by FTEXT                   DESC:   equ 1DA6h           ; sort downwards                   FIDX:   equ 1DA7h           ; field to sort or add up                   CNT:    equ 1DA8h           ; cards counted (word)                   TOTAL:  equ 1DAAh           ; their sum (4 bytes)                   FTEXT:  equ 1DAEh           ; text for FIND                   WPOS:   equ 1DB0h           ; a card being worked on                   NPTR:   equ 1DB2h           ; a field name, or the best card in SORT                   P1:     equ 1DB4h           ; the two sides of COMPARE                   P2:     equ 1DB6h                   WID:    equ 1DB8h           ; column widths for LIST (8 bytes)                   CONDS:  equ 1DC0h           ; 4 x 5 bytes: field, mask, AND/OR, value                   BUF:    equ 1E00h           ; a card being swapped                   S0:     equ 1F00h           ; stack (monitor uses 1Fxx)                            org 0400h                    ; ---------------------------------------------------------------- cards                    ;                    ; COMP80 QUEST                   ;                   ; An adventure engine with its own little language, for the PSI COMP80, in                   ; the 2 KB of ROM (0400h-0BFFh) that held BURP.  The monitor (0000h-03FFh)                   ; is unchanged.  As with BURP, the RS key enters it: the monitor's NMI                   ; handler jumps to 0800h.                   ;                   ; A world is typed in a line at a time, each line starting with one of                   ;   ROOM name description           the first ROOM is where the game starts                   ;   EXIT room direction room [IF flag]   a way out, usable while flag is set                   ;   OBJ name room description       something that can be carried                   ;   FIX name room description       something that can't                   ;   ON verb [noun] [IF condition AND condition ...] THEN action; action ...                   ; Conditions: HAVE obj, AT room, HERE obj (carried or in this room), a                   ; flag's name (set by SET), and NOT in front of any of them.  Actions: SAY                   ; text, SET flag, MOVE obj room (ME: carried; a word that is no room: out of                   ; the game), GO room, SCORE n, WIN, DIE and LOOK.                   ; Commands: PLAY, LIST, UNDO (forgets the last line), NEW.                   ;                   ; Words are matched by their first 4 letters.  A one-letter direction or                   ; verb in the world matches any word starting with that letter, so N matches                   ; NORTH.  In play, a command is a verb and a noun.  The rules for the verb                   ; come first: the first whose conditions hold runs, instead of anything                   ; else.  Then the built-in verbs: LOOK (L), INVENTORY (I), TAKE (GET), DROP,                   ; SCORE, QUIT, then the exits from the room; GO is left out (GO N is N).                   ;                   ; The world is kept as it was typed: each line its text and 0Dh, from 0C04h                   ; up to TXTEND.  PLAY makes a table of the objects (each the line it is on,                   ; and where it is now: a pointer to a room's name, or 0 when carried), and                   ; SET adds to a table of flags (pointers to their names), so the text itself                   ; is never changed.  Rooms, exits and rules are read from the text.                   ;                   ; Keys and screen are handled as in COMP80 FORTH: the monitor's NMI handler                   ; echoes each key and wakes the HALT in RAWKEY; RS while waiting is a rubout                   ; and RS at any other time (re)starts QUEST, keeping the world.  Line 0                   ; shows QUEST; lines 1-31 scroll.                    VRAM:   equ 8000h                   CLS64:  equ 0393h           ; monitor: spaces from 8040h to the end of the screen                   PAD64:  equ 03C4h           ; monitor: spaces at (DE) up to the next line                    MAGIC:  equ 0C00h           ; MAGICV when the world below is valid                   TXTEND: equ 0C02h           ; end of the world's text                   TEXT:   equ 0C04h           ; first line                   MAGICV: equ 0A55Bh                   TOP:    equ 1C00h           ; the text ends below here                   OBJT:   equ 1C00h           ; 32 objects: line, where (4 bytes each)                   FLAGT:  equ 1C80h           ; 32 flags: name (2 bytes each)                   TIB:    equ 1D00h           ; input line (80 bytes; page aligned)                   CURS:   equ 1DA0h           ; output position in screen memory                   NOBJ:   equ 1DA2h           ; number of objects                   NFLAG:  equ 1DA3h           ;   flags                   STATE:  equ 1DA5h           ; 0 playing, 1 won, 2 died                   SCORE:  equ 1DAAh                   ROOMP:  equ 1DACh           ; the room the player is in: its name                   VERB:   equ 1DAEh           ; the words typed                   NOUN:   equ 1DB0h                   LP:     equ 1DB2h           ; the rule being tried                   S0:     equ 1F00h           ; stack (monitor uses 1Fxx)                            org 0400h                    ;                    ; COMP80 APL                   ;                   ; A small APL for the PSI COMP80, in the 2 KB of ROM (0400h-0BFFh) that held                   ; BURP.  The monitor (0000h-03FFh) is unchanged.  As with BURP, the RS key                   ; enters it: the monitor's NMI handler jumps to 0800h.                   ;                   ; The keyboard has no APL characters, so the functions are spelt in ASCII:                   ;   + - * %          add, subtract, times, divide; monadic - negates                   ;   = # < > <= >=    comparisons, giving 1 or 0 (# is not equal)                   ;   MAX              the larger (MAX/ is the largest)                   ;   A MOD B          the remainder of A divided by B                   ;   IOTA N           1 to N                   ;   RHO B, A RHO B   the shape of B; B reshaped to A (N, or R C)                   ;   A / B            each element of B repeated A times (A of 1s and 0s                   ;                    picks some out)                   ;   F/ B  F! B       reduce and scan (APL's / and \) with a scalar F                   ;   A .F B           outer product (APL's jot-dot)                   ;   V[I]             indexing, from 1; the result has the shape of I                   ;   X: expression    assignment, to a single letter, A-Z                   ;   "TEXT"           a character vector                   ; A function takes everything to its right, as in APL: 2*3+4 is 14.  The                   ; operands are read from the left, so an assignment within a line counts                   ; only to its left.  Numbers are 16-bit integers; negative ones print with                   ; -.  % and MOD work on the sizes of negative numbers.  A line that isn't an                   ; assignment prints its value.  ) on a line of its own forgets all the                   ; variables.                   ;                   ; Arrays are rank 0, 1 or 2.  Each has a header: type (rank in bits 0-1,                   ; 80h for characters), rows, columns, number of elements, then the elements,                   ; a word each.  A vector is one row and a scalar one row of one, and a                   ; result of one element is always a scalar.  The values of the variables                   ; are kept from the bottom of the heap up to VTOP, each new one on the end                   ; (and ) starts afresh when it is full).  The values worked out on a line go                   ; down from the top of the heap (TMP), and are thrown away at the end of                   ; the line.                   ;                   ; Most functions make their result an element at a time: they set up the                   ; result's shape, and BUILD calls a routine (IY) for each element number.                   ;                   ; Keys and screen are handled as in COMP80 FORTH: RS while waiting is a                   ; rubout, and any key while a line is being worked out resets to the                   ; monitor; RS comes back with the variables kept.                    VRAM:   equ 8000h                   CLS64:  equ 0393h           ; monitor: spaces from 8040h to the end of the screen                   PAD64:  equ 03C4h           ; monitor: spaces at (DE) up to the next line                    MAGIC:  equ 0C00h           ; MAGICV when the variables below are valid                   VTOP:   equ 0C02h           ; end of the variables' values                   VTAB:   equ 0C04h           ; A-Z: a word each, the value or 0                   CURS:   equ 0C38h           ; output position in screen memory                   TMP:    equ 0C3Ah           ; bottom of this line's values                   FN:     equ 0C3Ch           ; the scalar function being applied                   FM:     equ 0C3Dh           ; 3 for an outer product                   TYP:    equ 0C3Eh           ; type being printed                   WID:    equ 0C3Fh           ; width of the numbers being printed                   PR:     equ 0C40h           ; where the next element of a result goes                   NA:     equ 0C42h           ; rows, or the left count ...                   NB:     equ 0C44h           ; ... and columns, or the right count                   CNT:    equ 0C46h                   LV:     equ 0C48h           ; left argument                   RV:     equ 0C4Ah           ; right argument                   NBUF:   equ 0C4Ch           ; a number as text (7 bytes)                   HEAP0:  equ 0C54h                   HEAPE:  equ 1D00h                   TIB:    equ 1D00h           ; input line (80 bytes; page aligned)                   S0:     equ 1F00h           ; stack (the monitor uses 1Fxx)                   MAGICV: equ 0A91Ch                    NSCAL:  equ 12              ; functions 0-11 are scalar                   F_SUB:  equ 1                   F_EQ:   equ 4                            org 0400h                    ; ---------------------------------------------------------------- parser                   ; DE is the text pointer throughout.
